title: Shoreline Cloud x Redwood: Partner Intro & Discovery
next_steps: Redwood to send partner one-pager, pricing ranges, and partner program terms (Maya)
Schedule SE-led technical deep dive to map infra and network requirements (Liam + Evan)
Share SOC 2 / security posture doc and high level SSO/KMS integration notes (Maya)
Customer to provide expected QPS, model types, and preferred regions for initial pilot (Evan)
action_items: Maya Chen: Send partner deck, pricing overlay, and draft MOU by 2026-04-02
Liam Patel: Propose available slots for technical deep dive and share checklist for benchmark run by 2026-04-06

summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Shoreline Cloud. Shoreline is a regional cloud/GPU provider evaluating partner models: reseller vs integration. Key themes: private deployments, network egress/peering, dedicated capacity for predictable latency, and pilot benchmark scope. Next steps: send partner materials, schedule SE deep dive, Shoreline to share model/QPS targets.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time — I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, AE on the partnerships team. With me is Liam, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:12] Priya (CTO, Shoreline): Doing well, thanks. Excited to chat — Carlos and Evan here.
[00:18] Carlos (Partnerships): Hi, yeah thanks for the invite. We wanted to understand how Redwood thinks about partner integrations and where Shoreline could plug in.
[00:28] Maya: Great, high-level we'll do intros, a quick overview of Redwood, then Liam will do a few technical clarifying q's. We want to understand Shoreline's goals — reseller, close integration, or joint go-to-market?
[00:40] Priya: Our initial thought is reseller + tight infra integration. We run GPU pools across three regions, want to offer a managed inference product to our customers, maybe white labeled. Main things: latency guarantees, multi-tenancy/srv isolation, and security controls (KMS, audit logs).
[00:58] Liam (SE): cool, can you talk a bit about the infra shape — what GPUs, networking, and whether you support private peering or VPC-to-VPC?
[01:06] Evan (Infra): yeah we mainly run A100 and H100-class instances, mix of 80GB and 40GB. We have direct cloud interconnects in us-west-2, eu-west-1; we support VPC peering and private links. Egress tends to be the cost knob for us.
[01:25] Maya: perfect, that's helpful. A couple of common asks we hear: does Shoreline want Redwood Dedicated-style reserved capacity (predictable throughput) vs letting customers hit hosted endpoints?
[01:35] Carlos: Ideally we want a product our sales org can sell: reserved capacity under Shoreline, with predictable SLAs. However, we also want the option to route overflow to Redwood hosted or our own burst capacity.
[01:47] Liam: that's doable — Redwood supports mixed routing policies: pin to dedicated pools, fallback to hosted variants, and you can set cost vs latency rules. Quick question on telemetry — what level of observability do you need surfaced to your console? Token-level costs, latency percentiles, per-model dashboards?
[02:04] Priya: all of the above. The team wants to be able to show customers cost breakdowns and SLOs; we also need audit logs for compliance.
[02:12] Maya: perfect. On compliance, Redwood has SOC 2, supports customer-managed KMS for private deployments, and SAML SSO via enterprise SSO providers. We can share the security pack.
[02:23] Carlos: perfect, please send that. Also curious on model types — do you support custom model onboarding and quantized variants?
[02:30] Liam: yes. We onboard customer models, and our runtime supports quantized execution paths and kernel selection to optimize for different sequence lengths. For partner models you can host them on Dedicated or Private installs. We do suggest an initial calibration run to pick quantization and batching settings.
[02:46] Evan: for the pilot, we run a mix of Llama-3 70B-ish and smaller encoder models for embeddings. Typical session lengths are 256–1024 tokens. QPS per tenant will start low, maybe 5–20 qps, but could spike. Any special network constraints for the KV cache traffic?
[03:02] Liam: kv cache is usually within the inference host; if you do multi-node KV sharing there's extra network chatter but it's manageable. For the spike handling, we can suggest autoscale + burst buckets.
[03:12] Maya: a few commercial topics — we have partner reseller discounts and margins; also we do committed reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated. Carlos, is Shoreline looking for revenue share or purely resale?
[03:22] Carlos: revenue share would be interesting, but we need to see margins vs cost. If Redwood can offer a partner tier and help with go-to-market credits that's a plus.
[03:32] Priya: also legal — we'll need an MOU and basic terms, plus indemnities and data residency clauses for European customers.
[03:39] Maya: understood. We'll circulate a partner overview + MOU draft. For EU data residency, Redwood Dedicated or Private deploy can live in customer-controlled VPCs; we can surface controls.
[03:50] Evan: curious about benchmarking — can Redwood run a benchmark on our infra or do we need to run it ourselves? Latency is a big selling point for our customers.
[03:58] Liam: we can do both. Typical flow: you provide model binaries and traffic profile, we'll run a benchmark (with your infra access or remote) and return p99/p50 latency, throughput, and cost per token. There's a checklist for perf runs — we'll share.
[04:12] Priya: what's the latency tradeoff when you use quantized models or smaller GPUs vs H100?
[04:18] Liam: quantization can reduce memory and sometimes improve throughput, but latency depends on kernel support. On H100 you'll see best single-stream latency; on A100 with the right kernels and batching you can get close. There's always a tradeoff: aggressive batching improves overall throughput but can increase tail latency. We usually tune batching windows per SLO.
[04:36] Carlos: any competitors you work with in the partner space?
[04:39] Maya: we've seen partners use Lambda, Paperspace; larger clouds like AWS obviously compete but also partner on infra.
[04:45] Evan: networking/cost — can Redwood's runtime be deployed as an appliance in our datacenter?
[04:50] Liam: Redwood Private does exactly that — private control plane, on-prem package if required. You run the inference nodes behind your network; Redwood can integrate with your KMS and your monitoring.
[04:59] Priya: good. Ok quick clarification on ticketing/SLAs for partner customers — do you offer white-labeled support or do customers go through Redwood?
[05:06] Maya: we support flexible support models: direct Redwood support with white-label options for partners on higher tiers; partners can also handle first-line support. We can detail support SLAs in the partner booklet.
[05:16] Carlos: great. I think we have enough to scope next step items. Evan will gather model list and QPS, we want the partner deck and security docs from you, and then we'll plan a technical deep dive to align infra.
[05:29] Maya: sounds good. Liam, anything you want to add?
[05:31] Liam: just that for the technical deep dive we'll want access to a small test cluster or a sample VM with networking settings so we can run a drift-free benchmark; also a list of network ACLs and egress estimates.
[05:43] Evan: noted. We'll get that together.
[05:46] Priya: timeline — we'd like a pilot ready in 6–8 weeks if the terms look right.
[05:51] Maya: totally reasonable. We'll aim to get materials and proposed deep-dive windows in the next week. Thanks everyone.
[05:58] Carlos: thanks, talk soon.
[06:00] [meeting end]
